Tracking down key dates for Singapore's first Olympic medallist — gathering sourced facts in order.I've confirmed the basic timeline — now opening detailed sources to fill in turning points and legacy.I've mapped the career arc — now verifying exact figures and honours before compiling the final list.1933 | Tan Howe Liang was born on 5 May 1933 in Swatow, Guangdong, China.
1937 | He moved with his family from Swatow to Singapore at around age 4 and settled in Chinatown.
1952 | He joined the Evergreen Weightlifting Party in 1952 and trained with a single set of barbells.
1953 | After 1 year of training he won the National Junior and Senior titles in the lightweight division at age 20.
1954 | He placed fourth at the Asian Games in Manila in 1954.
1956 | He finished ninth at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics after losing consciousness during the competition.
1958 | He lifted 157 kg in the clean-and-jerk and won lightweight gold with a 358 kg total at the 1958 Commonwealth and Empire Games in Cardiff.
1958 | He won lightweight gold with a 375 kg total at the 1958 Asian Games in Tokyo.
1959 | He won lightweight gold with a 369 kg total at the first SEAP Games in Bangkok in 1959.
1960 | On 8 September 1960 he finished second among 35 competitors in the lightweight division at Rome with a 380 kg total and a 155 kg clean-and-jerk.
1961 | He competed in the middleweight category for the first time at the 1961 SEAP Games in Rangoon and won silver.
1962 | He won middleweight gold with a 390 kg total at the 1962 Commonwealth Games in Perth.
1962 | He received the Pingat Jasa Gemilang (Meritorious Service Medal) at the 1962 National Day Awards.
1968 | He was appointed national weightlifting coach in 1968.
1982 | He began work with the Singapore Sports Council as a gymnasium supervisor in 1982 at the National Stadium.
1984 | He received the International Weightlifting Federation Gold Award in 1984.
2008 | He remained Singapore's only Olympic medallist for 48 years until the women's table tennis team won silver in 2008.
2024 | He died on 3 December 2024 at age 91.
